chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid. He said: Sahl ibn al-Marzuban al-Farisi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd ibn al-Mukhtar, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) went out one day while riding, and Ali (peace be upon him) went out walking alongside him. So he said to him: O Abu al-Hasan! Either ride or turn back, for God, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me that you should ride when I ride, walk when I walk, and sit when I sit — except when it is a limit from the limits of God that requires you to stand or be seated in it. God has not honoured me with an honour except that He has honoured you with its like. He distinguished me with prophethood and the mission and made you my wali in that — you uphold His commandments and manage His difficult affairs. By He who truly sent Muhammad as a prophet: he who denies you has not believed in me; he who repudiates you has not accepted me; and he who disbelieves in you has not believed in God. Your virtue is from my virtue, and my grace to you is the grace of God. And this is the saying of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic:
"Say, in the grace of God and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate." [Quran 10:58]

For the grace of God is the prophethood of your Prophet, and His mercy is the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib. "In that" — meaning, in prophethood and wilaya — "let them rejoice" — meaning, the Shi'a — "it is better than what they accumulate" — meaning, their opponents with their families, their wealth, and their children in this world. By God, O Ali! You were not created except so that your Lord may be worshipped, so that through you the landmarks of religion may be known, and through you the path of study may be rectified. He who has strayed has strayed from you, and no one shall be guided to God, the Mighty and Majestic, who is not guided to you and to your wilaya. And this is the saying of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic:
"And indeed I am most forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, then follows guidance." [Quran 20:82]

— meaning, to your guardianship (wilaya). And indeed my Lord, Blessed and Exalted, commanded me to impose of your right what He imposed of my right, and indeed your right is obligatory upon whoever believes in me. And were it not for you, the Party of God (Hizb Allah) would not be known, and through you the enemy of God is known. And whoever meets Him without your wilaya, he meets Him with nothing. And God, Almighty and Majestic, revealed to me:

"O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord" — meaning, regarding your guardianship (wilaya), O Ali — "and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message." [Quran 5:67, with tafsir interpolation]

And if I had not conveyed what I was commanded of your guardianship (wilaya), my deeds would have been rendered void. And whoever meets God, Almighty and Majestic, without your wilaya, his deeds are indeed rendered void — this is a promise that shall be fulfilled for me. And I say only the word of my Lord, Blessed and Exalted; and indeed what I say is from God, Almighty and Majestic, Who revealed it concerning you.

key_terms.حَبِطَ: Nullified, rendered void — said of deeds that become worthless due to a fundamental deficiency in faith
key_terms.حَدُّ اللَّهِ: A limit or ordinance of God — a religious boundary or prescribed duty that must be observed
key_terms.حِزْبُ اللَّهِ: Party of God — the community of true believers who follow the Imam
key_terms.فَضْل: Grace, favour, excellence — used here to equate the Prophet's grace with the grace of God toward Ali
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilaya — divine guardianship, spiritual authority, the special bond of Imam Ali with the Prophet and the Muslim community

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to Imam Ali about wilaya and its centrality to faith?
ai.summary: This is a lengthy prophetic hadith narrated through Imam al-Baqir and his ancestors in which the Prophet (SAWW) addresses Imam Ali (AS) directly, declaring that Ali's virtue mirrors his own, that wilaya (guardianship) of Ali is inseparable from belief in the Prophet, and that three Quranic verses (10:58, 20:82, 5:67) specifically refer to the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib. The hadith was transmitted within the context of early Shia communities of Kufa and Qom who understood wilaya as a doctrinal pillar of Islam, equivalent in importance to prophethood itself. This narration is characteristic of al-Amali literature — dictated in a single session by Shaykh al-Saduq — and reflects the Imami theological position that acceptance of Ali's wilaya is a condition of valid faith.
